reason: The text depicts the Israelite people being explicitly antagonistic toward King Rehoboam. When he rejects their petition to lighten the tax burden (responding harshly instead), they reject him outright, saying 'What share have we in David?' and telling him to look to his own house. They then stone to death Rehoboam's official Adoram, abandon Rehoboam as king, and make Jeroboam king over Israel instead. This constitutes clear antagonism from the regular people toward their leader.
